value.title: PRD 001: pij community
value.summary: A pij community is a project's agents operating as one cohesive fleet across many concurrent tasks. Its directory names every role, specialist and general, with its scope, holders, memory and outputs, so roles outlive seats and the community builds knowledge over time.

sections.name: why
sections.value: Splitting work across focused seats keeps each context small. Small contexts make agents sharper and faster and cost less, because cost grows roughly with the square of the context. Today pij knows a handful of roles (prime, pm, pa, worker), and projects improvise specialists: brief files in one project, inline prompts that vanish in another. A specialist's knowledge dies with its seat, results are buried in messages, and nothing tells a coder that Docker work belongs to someone else. A community directory makes roles durable: a role outlives its seats, its knowledge grows across them, and work and results flow through it.

value.name: prime
value.need: An operating picture of the community and prompts on what to fix next.

value.name: pm
value.need: To staff its own work with coders and reviewers and route owned work to specialists.

value.name: pa
value.need: To keep seats healthy without losing what they learned.

value.name: worker seat
value.need: To be told its job, what it may touch, and where to send work it does not own.

value.name: requester
value.need: To get a result back in the way it chose, without stalling.

value.name: operator
value.need: A fleet that gets better at its project over time and costs less.

value.goal: A role outlives the seats that hold it.
Knowledge accumulates per role, in git, indexed by flowspace.
Owned work reaches its owner without anyone policing it.
Results are durable records, not messages.
The prime runs the community from one view that tells it what to do next.

value.text: Cross-machine communities. Out of scope, but nothing here may block them (req-17).
Copying transcripts between machines; flowspace already holds conversation history.
pij starting or reviving seats on its own.

value.title: One community directory per project
value.statement: Each project has one community directory, bound to the project path the same way a prime is. It lists every role, its scope, its holders, its memory and its outputs.
value.done_when: `pij directory` run inside a project shows that project's roles and nothing from another project.

value.title: Directory files live on the governance branch
value.statement: Role definitions, role memory, outputs, the routing table and external entries live under `<government-root>/community/`. When governance is not set up, every directory verb refuses by name and points at the setup step; it never falls back to another location.
value.done_when: With no government root, `pij directory add x` exits with the named refusal and a runnable next step; with one, the file appears under `community/roles/x/`.

value.title: pij is the only writer
value.statement: Directory files are written only through pij verbs. pij writes the JSON, runs `ddocs validate` and `ddocs build` by absolute path, and commits on the governance branch. The store keeps a pointer (project id, repo-relative path, commit). pij never pushes. A missing `ddocs` gives a named refusal, and `just doctor` checks for it.
value.done_when: Each verb produces one governance commit whose `.dd.json` validates clean and whose `.dd.md` is regenerated; with `ddocs` off PATH the verb refuses by name.

value.title: Role definitions are pij/role ddocs
value.statement: A role definition holds: id, title, kind (specialist or general), lifecycle (long-lived or per-task), holders (one or many), scope, out of scope, forbidden paths, default seat (harness, model, effort), inputs, output kinds, standing packet, template and version it came from, and a changelog.
value.done_when: `ddocs validate` passes on a role created from each shipped template, and fails on one missing scope or standing packet.

value.title: Anyone may change the directory; every change is attributed
value.statement: Any seat may create, edit, assign or release. pij does not gate these by role. Every change records who made it and why in the role's changelog.
value.done_when: A worker seat can assign itself to a role, and the role's changelog shows its seat id and reason.

value.title: Assign, release and lineage
value.statement: `pij directory assign <role> <seat>` and `release` bind and unbind seats. Lineage records every holder: seat id, harness session id, machine, from and to. Assigning a second live seat to a one-holder role warns but does not block. `pij close` still tombstones the seat and also ends its assignment.
value.done_when: After assign, release, assign of another seat and a close, lineage shows both seats with their session ids, machine and times.

value.title: Send to a role
value.statement: `pij send role:<id>` delivers only when exactly one live seat holds the role. With none, it refuses with runnable commands: revive the last holder, or start a fresh seat assigned to the role. With two or more, it refuses and lists the live seats. pij never starts a seat on its own.
value.done_when: Three tests (0, 1 and 2 live holders) give a named refusal with commands, a delivery, and a named refusal listing both seats.

value.title: The requester chooses how it hears back
value.statement: `--reply wake|fyi|none` on a send to a role, default `wake`, is stored on the request. The output that answers it notifies with that mode. A `block` verdict or a `failed` result always wakes. An output nobody requested goes as an FYI to the nearest seat above (its PM, else the prime). There is only ever one recipient.
value.done_when: An idle requester that sent with the default is woken by the output; one that sent `--reply fyi` is not woken; a block verdict wakes a `fyi` requester.

value.title: Role memory is prompted before compact and close
value.statement: Before pij compacts or closes a seat that holds a role, it first asks the seat to add what it learned to `community/roles/<id>/memory/`, and runs the compact or close after that turn. A seat with nothing new replies that it has nothing to add.
value.done_when: A compact of a role holder shows the memory prompt turn first, then the compact; a seat holding no role is compacted directly.

value.title: Outputs are records
value.statement: `pij output verdict|deliverable|note --subject <address> ...` writes one ddoc per output under `community/roles/<id>/outputs/<yyyy-mm>/`, and records a store fact. A subject naming a docs path is checked against main when written. The daemon writes outputs one at a time. `pij outputs --role --subject` reads from the store.
value.done_when: Two seats writing outputs at once produce two commits and two files with no conflict; `pij outputs --subject pr:N` returns the latest verdict with its head sha.

value.title: Routing table
value.statement: pij builds a routing table from every role's scope, writes it to `community/ROUTES.md`, and sends it to a seat when it is assigned to a role, after a compact, when a revived seat returns, and on demand (`pij directory routes`). When routes change, only the changed rows go as an FYI to the project's live seats. A change of holder sends nothing.
value.done_when: Adding a role with a scope regenerates ROUTES.md and sends one FYI with the new row to each live seat in the project; reassigning a holder sends nothing.

value.title: The prime's operating picture
value.statement: `pij directory` shows each role with holders, waiting requests, latest output and memory freshness, and prompts the prime with next actions, in the style of `harness flow orient`: no live holder with requests waiting, two live holders on a one-holder role, memory not updated across recent closes, a recommended role missing.
value.done_when: Each of the four conditions, set up in a test project, produces its prompt with a runnable command.

value.title: Versioned role templates
value.statement: pij ships role templates, each with a version. `pij directory add <id> --from template:<name>` copies one onto the governance branch, where it is edited freely. When a template moves ahead, `pij directory` shows the difference and never applies it automatically. Templates are written fresh for the public repo.
value.done_when: A role taken from template v1 shows a diff after the template moves to v2, and its local edits are untouched.

value.title: Core roles and the security reminder
value.statement: Creating a directory creates the core roles: prime, pm, pa, coder, reviewer. pij prompts the prime until a security role exists. Optional templates include devcontainer, researcher, note-taker, topic expert, docs-keeper, infra, release, test and QA, designer and transcriber.
value.done_when: A new directory lists the five core roles and a security prompt; adding `security` clears the prompt.

value.title: Skill route for communities
value.statement: The pij skill gets a community route that teaches the prime to set up and run the community, the PM to assign and release seats for its own work, and the PA to see memory written before compacts. Worker seats are only told what to do through their packets.
value.done_when: The route exists, is token-lean, and a fresh prime following it sets up a directory with core roles and a security role.

value.title: External entries
value.statement: The prime may add an external entry to record a seat borrowed from another project. Loans are not otherwise tracked.
value.done_when: `pij directory external add` writes a dated note under `community/external.dd.json`.

value.title: Cross-machine work is not precluded
value.statement: Git is the shared copy; each machine's store is a local index rebuildable from the governance branch. Lineage records the machine. Transcripts never move between machines.
value.done_when: Deleting the store's directory index and rebuilding from the branch gives the same `pij directory` output.

value.title: Project docs system
value.statement: PRDs and blueprints live in `docs/project/NNN-<slug>/`; roadmaps in `docs/project/roadmaps/`. They use the `pij/prd`, `pij/blueprint` and `pij/roadmap` schemas and are joined by ddocs link cells: roadmap steps deliver requirement rows and build components, and components realise rows.
value.done_when: `ddocs validate` is clean at default depth on this PRD, its blueprint and roadmap 001; `ddocs graph` draws roadmap to PRD to blueprint.

value.title: No per-tick cost
value.statement: Every directory write and notification happens per request or per change, never on a timer and never per seat per tick. The cost of writes and route FYIs is measured on the live fleet before merge.
value.done_when: The plan's backpressure carries a cost row with before and after readings from `pij-rs --json ping` and `just spawn-rate`.

value.question: Budgets, checkpoints and heartbeats for per-task specialists: a time or turn limit, forced partial writes, and visible progress.
How roles link to roadmap steps, so the directory can say which steps need a role that does not exist.
value.default: Next workshop, with PRD and roadmap prompting.

value.question: Do route changes go to every live seat in the project, or only to the prime?
value.default: Every live seat, as an FYI.

value.question: When does pij's existing PRD register move from the governance folder into docs/project?
value.default: A separate step after this PRD is accepted.
